newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain's Clarke optimistic on post-97 Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke optimistic on post-97 Hong Kong.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday he was reasonably optimistic that Hong Kong would remain a financial centre after its transfer of sovereignty to China this year.

"I think it certainly needs to, it must do and I'm reasonably optimistic but obviously everything depends...upon the continuation of the financial framework that's always existed here that enabled Hong Kong to be such a fantastic success," Clarke said in an interview with government radio.
"But everything else depends on whether the rule of law and the conditions that make it so attractive for international investment," he said.

Clarke, who flew in late on Thursday to attend a one-day conference organised by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, also said countries in the IMF wanted Hong Kong to stay financially important.
"Yes, I think it's one of the most important issues facing the countries that comprise the IMF to ensure that Hong Kong does remain a financial centre after the changeover," he said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over 150 years, would revert to Chinese rule at midnight June 30.
Under joint Sino-British treaties on Hong Kong's handover, it is promised a high degree of autonomy for the next 50 years.
